caption_instagram:
Since 21 November 2025, gratuity is governed by the Code on Social Security, 2020. Here's what every employee should know. 💼

✅ Regular employees: eligible after 5 years of continuous service
⏳ Fixed-term employees: eligible after just 1 year (proportionate)
🕊️ No minimum service needed in case of death or disablement
🧮 Amount: 15 days' wages for every completed year of service
💰 Maximum: ₹20 lakh (as currently notified)
📊 If allowances exceed 50% of your pay, the excess is added back to wages
📅 Employer must pay within 30 days of it becoming due; delay attracts simple interest
📝 Keep your nominee updated

caption_linkedin:
The four Labour Codes came into force on 21 November 2025, and gratuity is now governed by the Code on Social Security, 2020. Key points for employees and HR teams:

• Eligibility: five years of continuous service for regular employees; not required on death or disablement
• Fixed-term employees: eligible after one year of continuous service, on a proportionate basis
• Amount: 15 days' wages for every completed year of service
• Ceiling: ₹20 lakh, as currently notified by the Central Government
• Wages: where allowances exceed 50% of total remuneration, the excess is added back to wages — which can raise the gratuity base
• Timeline: the employer must pay within 30 days of gratuity becoming payable; delayed payment attracts simple interest
• Nomination: on an employee's death, gratuity is paid to the nominee, or to legal heirs if there is none
